gallery.title: File:Wurttflag.png
gallery.credit:
Own work - 
Below is a list with written sources referring to this flag
Swabisches Chronik, 5th of August 1803 - "[...] wurde oben in der Residenz die dreifarbige Württembergische fahnen aufgezogen." 
(The tricolor Württemberg flag was raised at the top of the residence.)
Matthison, Friedrich von. Das Dianenfest bei Bebenhausen. 1813 - "Schauf auf der Emichsburg ihr hoch, Die Königsflagge wehn? [...]" 
(Look up at the Emichsburg, the royal flag is flying?)
Memminger, Johann Daniel Georg von. Stuttgart und Ludwigsburg, mit ihrer Umgebung, Germany: Stuttgart, 1817. - "Auf dem Alten Schlosse weht eine große dreyfarbige fahne, die aber, wenn König sich aud der Residenz enrfernt, eingezogen wird und betzwegen zum zeichen seiner abwesenheit dient." (On the Old Castle flies a large tricolor flag, which, however, is taken down when the King leaves the residence and serves as a symbol of his absence.)
In reference to the Emichsburg: 
[...] die staatliche fahne die während der anwesenheit des Königs auf ihrem thurme weht, [...] (the state flag that flies on its tower during the presence of the King.)
Unknown author, Watercolor of Stuttgart, 1815. -  
Eine Fähne welche aufgestecht wird sobald Ihre Majestät in der Stadt sind.
[...] die flagge zeigt die Kgl. Farben unter König friedrich. (A flag that is raised as soon as His Majesty is in town. [...] The flag shows the royal colors under King Frederick)
Many contemporary depictions show the flags mentioned in these excerpts, most famously, a painting by Johann Baptist Seele.
The usage of the words Staatliche (stately) most possibly indicates that the colors were used as the "Landesfarben" (national colors) of the country, something that can be confirmed in the following excerpt:
Starklof, Richard. Geschichte des kgl. württembergischen zweiten Reiter-Regiments, ehemaligen Jäger-Regiments zu Pferde Herzog Louis, Germany:Eduard Zernin, 1862. - 

Seit Beginn des Jahres 1810 trugen die württembergischen Truppen (durch allerh. Ordre vom 1 Januar) auf der linken Seite des Huts , Kaskets , der Bärenmüze u. s. w. unten am Federbusch in einer schwarz-roth-gelben Kokarde die württembergischen Landesfarben.  (Since the beginning of 1810, the Württemberg troops wore (by order of 1 January) on the left side of the hat, jacket, bearer's cap etc. at the bottom of the plume in a black, red and yellow cockade the Württemberg national colours.)

gallery.title: File:Archibald Alison, Paris and its environs, to illustrate the Battle of Paris, 30 March 1814, 1814 - David Rumsey.jpg
gallery.description:
An old map of Paris, France.
Engraved hand colored map. Inset: Country around Paris. Shows the position of the Allies and French cavalry, infantry and artillery. In lower right margin: W. & A.K. Johnston, Edinr. Relief shown by hachures

Atlas to accompany Alison's History of Europe: from the commencement of the French Revolution in 1789 to the restoration of the Bourbons in 1815. Atlas consists of a series of maps and plans that cover major military engagements during the French Revolution. Complete with 108 maps and plans, a frontispiece on military symbols and fortifications, and a glossary of military and marine terms. Maps engraved by W. & A.K. Johnston under the direction of Sir Archibald Alison. The maps cover Europe and her colonies in America, Africa and India. Bound in half calf over marbled-paper boards, with gilt-blocked label "Alison's history of Europe, Atlas" on spine.

gallery.title: File:Berlin, Kreuzberg Denkmal – West panel.jpg
gallery.description:
The Kreuzberg Memorial (1817-1821) commemorates the twelve most significant victories of the Wars of Liberation ('Befreiungskriege') having freed the German states from the napoléonic régime, and led to its collapse – and the abdication of their emperor on April 4th, 1814. 
The Allied Armies took Paris on March 30th, 1814.    

The "Grand Entry of the Allied Sovereigns into Paris", though its Saint-Martin Gate, took place on the next day, March 31st, 1814.
